drills.q: Why can't you compare a cosine similarity score between vectors from two different embedding models?
drills.a: Each model learns its own vector space during training with no guaranteed alignment; the score would be a number but a meaningless one.

drills.q: What is Matryoshka Representation Learning and why does it matter operationally?
drills.a: It trains a contrastive loss at multiple nested prefix lengths of the same vector so any prefix is a usable embedding, turning dimensionality into a runtime truncation knob instead of a model-selection decision.

drills.q: Walk through the cost of embedding a 10M-chunk, 250-tokens-average corpus with OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, and its full-precision storage footprint.
drills.a: 2.5B tokens * $0.13/1M = $325 one-time. Storage at 3072d fp32: 10M*3072*4 bytes ~= 123 GB before index overhead; truncating to 512d drops it to ~20.5 GB.

drills.q: A model card says to prefix queries with 'query: ' and passages with 'passage: '. What happens if you skip this, and how would you catch the bug?
drills.a: Retrieval quality silently degrades because query/passage vectors no longer sit in the geometric relationship the contrastive training established. Catch it with a recall@k regression test in CI, not manual inspection.

drills.q: Your team wants to switch from OpenAI text-embedding-3-small to Cohere embed-v4 for better multilingual coverage. What does this actually require?
drills.a: A full reindex: re-embed every chunk (incompatible vector spaces), rebuild the ANN index, shadow-evaluate recall@k and answer quality before cutover. Budget it as a migration project, not a config change.

drills.q: Why might quantization hurt recall more unpredictably than Matryoshka truncation, and would you ever combine both?
drills.a: Quantization is applied post-hoc with no trained guarantee of even tolerance across dimensions/models, unlike MRL's trained-in graceful degradation. You can combine both for extreme storage savings, but each stacked step needs its own recall@k validation -- losses aren't simply additive.

drills.q: Design the embedding strategy for a RAG system serving English and low-resource-language queries against a shared corpus under a strict latency budget.
drills.a: Check per-language coverage (not aggregate MTEB/MIRACL) against actual target languages since coverage is uneven; self-host a Matryoshka-truncated model for the query-embedding hop (on the critical path) rather than an API round trip; validate low-resource recall with its own eval set; consider translation-to-pivot-language as a fallback and say so explicitly.

drills.q: How would you decide the dimension to actually deploy for a given corpus, without guessing from a blog post?
drills.a: Build a labeled (or synthetic) eval set, embed the corpus at several candidate truncation dimensions, measure recall@k and nDCG at each, and deploy the smallest dimension where the metric plateaus.
